references.text: The blood of the Passover lamb on the doorposts protected the Israelites from the angel of death. Those who remained inside the house were safe, just as Rahab's family had to stay inside to be protected.
The blood as a sign of protection - those who were inside under the sign of the blood were spared, parallel to Rahab's house marked with the scarlet cord.
The principle that blood comes upon someone's head as a sign of guilt or responsibility for death.
Blood on one's own head as an expression of personal responsibility for one's own death, using the same legal terminology.
David declares himself and his house innocent (נְקִיִּם) in a similar formulation about responsibility and innocence.
The prophet's responsibility to warn - if he warns, he is innocent; the blood comes upon those who do not listen.
The expression 'let his blood come upon us' is used similarly regarding taking responsibility for someone's death.
Paul declares himself clean/innocent and says their blood will come upon their own heads, following the same principle of responsibility.
Paul declares himself innocent of everyone's blood because he has proclaimed the whole counsel of God, a similar freedom from liability.
